main_text.p: Alius est hellenismus, cum participio & verbo substantivo utimur pro verbo participij. Thuc. τῆς πόλεως τῆς Πλαταιέων ἐξελασθῆναι ὡς τῆς Ἀθηναίων ἀφίστασθαι, multitudini Platæensium non volenti erat ab Athenien-sibus deficere, id est, multitudo nolebat. Xenoph. ὡς δὲ ὁ τοῦ Ἀγησιλάου, ἀχθο-μένῳ ᾧ τα, erat autem non Agesilao ægré ferenti hæc, id est, Agesilaus non ægré ferebat hæc. Plat. εἰ σοι ἡδομένῳ ἔσῃ, si tibi lætanti est: id est, si placet tibi.
Sed ut verba, sic participia interdum redundant apud Atticos: ut, παίζεις ἔχων, pro παίζεις, ludis: τυγχάνει ὤν, est. Sic Demosthenes ἐχθρός γε ὢν ἐπιπρ-
ἐχθρός γε ὢν ἐπιπρ- [line continues on the next page in print; text uncertain]

page.notes: The Greek is only partly legible on the scan; words marked by [?] are uncertain, and the Greek accents may be inexact. The last line "ἐχθρός γε ὢν ἐπιπρ-" is a hyphenated line end, and the sentence continues on a page not shown. The first Greek word on the page is a fragment of a line from the previous page. The signature "x : iiij" is partly faint and may read differently. The footnote above is a duplicate of the last line and should be read as part of the main text, not as a separate note.
